detailed_rationale:
Nava Ltd (formerly Nava Bharat Ventures) is a ferro-alloys manufacturer (plants in Telangana and Odisha) with a 65%-owned Zambian subsidiary, Maamba Collieries, that runs the country's largest coal concession and a 300 MW power plant (~10% of Zambia's installed generation). Despite the quant sector tag of 'NotCyclical', this is in substance a commodity-and-merchant-power business -- ferro-alloy realisations track steel/global commodity cycles, and the Zambian coal-power operation carries kwacha FX and offtake-pricing exposure -- and it should be judged with that cyclicality in mind rather than at face value against the tag.

Q4 FY26 illustrates the volatility: consolidated net profit fell 45.8% YoY to Rs 127.13 cr despite revenue growing 12.2%, and the disclosed proximate cause was an extraordinary effective tax rate of 58.0% versus just 6.5% in the year-ago quarter -- a clear one-off tax item rather than an operating collapse. But the tax swing does not explain everything: profit also fell 42.7% sequentially even though revenue rose 15.3% QoQ, which is the second consecutive quarter of declining profitability and points to some genuine margin pressure alongside the tax anomaly (commodity realisations, Zambian power/coal pricing, or cost inflation -- the exact split was not disclosed in the sources reviewed). The stock fell over 10% on the print.

The quant data itself flags this deterioration -- the 1-year score (42.7) is markedly weaker than the 3-year score (57.9) -- consistent with a business whose recent trend is softer than its longer-run average. With moderate leverage (D/E 0.25, still comfortable interest cover of 143x) and a genuinely commodity-cyclical earnings stream, a PE of ~21x is not obviously supported by the current trajectory.
recommendation_rationale: Already a quant-Hold, and the weak 1-year score plus two consecutive quarters of declining profit (only partly explained by the disclosed tax anomaly) argue against treating this as a candidate for anything more constructive; nothing here is severe enough, or clean enough as a data-quality issue, to warrant escalation -- it reads as ordinary commodity-cycle volatility plus a one-off tax item.
summary: Nava combines a ferro-alloys manufacturing business with a Zambian coal-mining and power-generation operation -- both of which are more commodity-cyclical than the sector classification suggests. The most recent quarter's profit fell sharply, partly due to an unusually high one-off tax charge, but revenue and profit have also been softening for two consecutive quarters on an underlying basis. We rate this a Hold: the tax spike should reverse, but the broader trend needs to stabilise before this looks attractively priced.
positive_para: Diversified earnings base spanning Indian ferro-alloys and a large, strategically important Zambian coal-and-power asset (Maamba Collieries, ~10% of national generation), with comfortable leverage (D/E 0.25, interest cover 143x) and a 19.5% ROCE. The Q4 tax spike (58% effective rate vs 6.5% a year ago) looks like a one-off that should normalise, which would restore a meaningful chunk of reported profit going forward.
negative_para: Profit has now declined for two consecutive quarters even before accounting for the tax anomaly (Q4 profit fell 42.7% sequentially despite revenue rising 15.3% QoQ), and the 1-year quant score is notably weaker than the 3-year score -- both signs of a real, not just tax-driven, deterioration in the underlying trend. Ferro-alloy and Zambian coal/power economics are genuinely commodity-cyclical (despite the 'NotCyclical' sector tag), carrying steel-cycle and Zambian-kwacha FX exposure that can swing results materially either way.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~21x PE on a commodity-linked ferro-alloys-and-power business showing two quarters of underlying profit deterioration is not cheap -- it appears to assume the tax spike fully reverses and the softer operating trend stabilises. Given the genuine cyclicality of both the ferro-alloy and Zambian coal/power businesses, this reads as fair-to-slightly-rich rather than a value opportunity.
